question_text: Explain Belady's anomaly and discuss why the optimal page replacement algorithm cannot be utilized in practical operating systems.
correct_answer: Belady's anomaly is the unexpected phenomenon where increasing the number of allocated physical frames results in an increased number of page faults for certain replacement policies, notably First-In, First-Out (FIFO). The optimal page replacement algorithm (OPT) selects the victim page that will not be referenced for the longest period of time in the future, guaranteeing the lowest possible fault rate. It cannot be used in practical systems because the operating system cannot predict future program memory accesses in advance.

question_text: What is thrashing, and how does the working-set model detect and prevent it?
correct_answer: Thrashing is a state of severe performance degradation where the system spends the majority of its time moving pages back and forth between RAM and backing store rather than executing application code. This happens when processes are allocated fewer frames than their active working sets require. The working-set model monitors the set of pages each process references over a moving time window delta; if the sum of all working-set sizes exceeds total available physical frames, the OS suspends a process to free frames and restore normal throughput.
